steps.explanationAfterStep: A 4π electrocyclic ring opening: one σ and one π bond become two π bonds, and the ring strain is released. On heating, a four-electron system opens conrotatory: both ends turn the same way. From the cis-dimethylcyclobutene this puts one methyl outside and one inside, so the product is (2E,4Z)-hexa-2,4-diene; the trans isomer gives the (E,E)-diene. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges.

title: Ring opening of a cyclobutene
subtitle: cis-3,4-Dimethylcyclobutene opens conrotatory to (E,Z)-hexa-2,4-diene
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 35

cyclobutene.caption: cis-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene
hintTiers: A four-membered ring is strained. Which σ bond of the ring can break and give its electrons to a new π bond, with the old π bond moving across too?
The σ bond between the two carbons carrying the methyl groups breaks. Its pair makes a new C=C to one neighbour, and the old C=C pair moves to make a C=C on the other side. Two arrows.

Arrow 1: from the σ bond between the two methyl-bearing carbons to the ring bond between one of them and its alkene neighbour (a new π bond). Arrow 2: from the old C=C π bond to the bond between the other alkene carbon and the other methyl-bearing carbon.
cyclobutene.learnerPrompt: Heat opens the strained four-membered ring into a diene. Draw the single step.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That σ bond is next to the double bond. The bond that breaks is the one opposite it, between the two sp³ carbons that carry the methyl groups.
The methyl groups stay attached. The ring opens by breaking the ring σ bond between the two carbons that carry them.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the ring σ bond becomes a new π bond. Now the carbon that loses that σ bond needs a new bond, and the old C=C pair moves over to make it. One more arrow.

mechanismSummary: Cyclobutenes open on heating to buta-1,3-dienes, the reverse of a 4π electrocyclisation; ring strain makes the opening downhill. The rule for thermal electrocyclic reactions: 4n electrons go conrotatory, 4n + 2 go disrotatory. Here four electrons, so conrotatory, and cis-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene gives only (E,Z)-hexa-2,4-diene. Under light the rules swap. The app does not check stereochemistry yet, so the drawings carry no wedges.
